title: A contractible factor preserves universal localization
statement: Use small simplicial sets, degreewise products and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and universal localization of [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map]. Let $f:A\to B$ be universally localizing and let $C$ be a small weakly contractible simplicial set, meaning that $C\to\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then $A\times C\xrightarrow{\operatorname{pr}_A}A\xrightarrow f B$ is universally localizing. No Kan, quasicategory or finiteness hypothesis is imposed on $A,B,C$.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.5.12 (02M8), the contractible-factor composite; Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Since $C\to\Delta^0$ induces a bijection on components, $C$ has a vertex: otherwise every degree is empty, since every simplex has a vertex, so its realization has no components. Fix $c\in C_0$ once. Let $g:T\to B$ be an arbitrary small simplicial map, set $X=T\times_B A$, and write $h:X\to T$ for the projection. By [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map], choose $W\subseteq X_1$, independent of the target quasicategory, such that $h^*$ identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)$ with the full subcategory $\operatorname{Fun}_W(X,\mathcal E)$ for every quasicategory $\mathcal E$. Fix such $\mathcal E$ temporarily. Put $\mathcal D=\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$; it is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] to the weak homotopy equivalence $C\to\Delta^0$ and target $\mathcal D$ (the point is Kan). It gives an equivalence $\mathcal D\to\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(C,\mathcal D)$, namely the constant-diagram functor.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.5.12, expanded directly on the functor-category universal property using simplicial groupoid localization (Kerodon 6.3.1.21, tag 01MY).

proof.text: Let $p:X\times C\to X$, $s_c:X\to X\times C$, $x\mapsto(x,c)$, and let $V\subseteq(X\times C)_1$ consist of all edges $(s_0x,v)$ with $x\in X_0$, $v\in C_1$. Write $\mathcal L$ for the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(X\times C,\mathcal E)$ on diagrams inverting $V$. Currying and permutation of product coordinates identify $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(C,\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E))$ with $\mathcal L$. Explicitly an $n$-simplex on either side is a map $H:X\times C\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$. On the left, for every edge $v$ of $C$ and parameter vertex $i$, its image is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(X,\mathcal E)$, which by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] means exactly that $H$ sends $(s_0x,v,i)$ to an equivalence for every $x$. This is the condition on the vertices of $H$ defining the full subcategory on the right. Both descriptions restrict $H$ in the same parameter coordinate, hence agree in every simplicial degree and on all operators. The constant-diagram functor in step 1 becomes restriction $P=p^*:\mathcal D\to\mathcal L$, so $P$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.5.12, expanded directly on the functor-category universal property using simplicial groupoid localization (Kerodon 6.3.1.21, tag 01MY).

proof.text: Restriction $R=s_c^*:\mathcal L\to\mathcal D$ satisfies $RP=1_{\mathcal D}$ strictly. It is a quasi-inverse to $P$. Indeed choose a quasi-inverse $Q$ with natural equivalences $QP\simeq1_{\mathcal D}$ and $PQ\simeq1_{\mathcal L}$, as in the definition of functor equivalence in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Applying $R$ to the latter gives $Q=RPQ\simeq R$; applying $P$ gives $PQ\simeq PR$. Combining this with $PQ\simeq1_{\mathcal L}$ yields $PR\simeq1_{\mathcal L}$. Restriction, postcomposition and whiskering here are composition of the maps $H$ on products with $\Delta^n$, so these are actual coherent transformations. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] ensures the whiskered transformations are equivalences.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.5.12, expanded directly on the functor-category universal property using simplicial groupoid localization (Kerodon 6.3.1.21, tag 01MY).

proof.text: Define $U_g=V\cup\{(w,s_0c):w\in W\}\subseteq(X\times C)_1$ and let $\mathcal L_0=\operatorname{Fun}_{U_g}(X\times C,\mathcal E)$, a full subcategory of $\mathcal L$. Let $\mathcal D_0=\operatorname{Fun}_W(X,\mathcal E)$. The functor $P$ maps $\mathcal D_0$ into $\mathcal L_0$: it sends $V$ to degenerate edges and sends $(w,s_0c)$ to the image of $w$. Conversely $R$ maps $\mathcal L_0$ into $\mathcal D_0$, since $s_c$ sends $w$ exactly to $(w,s_0c)$. Thus $P$ and $R$ restrict to functors between these full subcategories. Their identity $RP=1$ restricts too. The natural equivalence $PR\simeq1_{\mathcal L}$ of step 3 restricts to $\mathcal L_0$: both its endpoint functors take values in $\mathcal L_0$, and every simplex of the transformation has only vertices in that subcategory. Fullness includes the transformation, its inverse and its two inverse-witness triangles. Therefore the restricted $P:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal L_0$ is an equivalence of whole functor quasicategories, with no restriction on the transformation edges.

source.place: Corollary 6.3.5.12, expanded directly on the functor-category universal property using simplicial groupoid localization (Kerodon 6.3.1.21, tag 01MY).

proof.text: There is a degreewise simplicial isomorphism $T\times_B(A\times C)\cong(T\times_B A)\times C=X\times C$, sending $(t,(a,z))$ to $((t,a),z)$ with the displayed inverse. Under it the pullback projection to $T$ is $hp$. Its restriction functor is exactly $P h^*$ on every parameter simplex. Step 1 makes $h^*:\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal E)\to\mathcal D_0$ an equivalence, and step 4 makes $P:\mathcal D_0\to\mathcal L_0$ an equivalence. To exhibit the composite equivalence explicitly, choose quasi-inverses \(Q_h\) to \(h^*\) and \(Q_P\) to the restricted \(P\), with their two coherent inverse equivalences. The composite \(Q_hQ_P\) is a quasi-inverse to \(P h^*\): whisker the equivalence \(Q_hh^*\simeq1\) by \(Q_P\), and compose it with the equivalence \(Q_P P\simeq1\); on the other side whisker \(P Q_P\simeq1\) by \(h^*\), and compose with \(h^*Q_h\simeq1\). The inverse-triangle witnesses are the corresponding composites, so the definition of functor equivalence applies. Hence $hp$ exhibits $T$ as the localization of $X\times C$ at $U_g$. The collection $U_g$ uses only $g,W,c$ and not $\mathcal E$, so it works simultaneously for every target. Since $g$ was arbitrary, [def-coef-universally-localizing-simplicial-map] proves the assertion. Empty $X$ or $T$ is included; no fibrancy of $A,B,C,T$ was used.

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches the node and Kerodon 6.3.5.12 (02M8). Hypotheses are the recorded IsUniversallyLocalizing and IsContractible; the conclusion is fst A C ≫ f; there is no extra Kan, quasicategory or finiteness assumption. Edge cases checked: C=Δ⁰, C=Δ¹, empty base change, f=𝟙; empty C is excluded. No other declaration states this; docstrings and blueprint tag present; proof only sorry. Fault: the file declared only `universe u`, so the test universe v of IsUniversallyLocalizing was generalised separately on hf (u_2) and the conclusion (u_3), as #check with pp.universes shows. That is an unbound universe and a universe-transfer claim stronger than the node. fixes/ContractibleFactorUniversalLocalization.lean declares `universe u v` and writes IsUniversallyLocalizing.{u, v} on both sides, plus one docstring sentence. Delivered and fixed files both compile clean through nt_compile.py; the fixed #check shows a single shared v; lean.statement is re-read by the refit.
